core_obligations: Reduce to the projective case (proof lines 5475-5487): a quasi-affine scheme is a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme, an affine scheme is the projective spectrum of a polynomial ring, and a scheme with an ample invertible sheaf is an open subscheme of a projective spectrum; hence it suffices to treat the case where X is a locally closed subscheme of a projective spectrum.

Cover the finite set (proof lines 5489-5498): since the standard opens form a basis and the set E is finite, choose finitely many homogeneous elements f_i such that E is contained in the union of the D_+(f_i) and that union avoids the complement T of X in its closure.

Produce a single standard open (proof lines 5500-5506): for the ideal generated by the f_i and the finitely many points of E, the graded lemma supplies a homogeneous element f in that ideal which lies in none of those points; then the standard open of f contains E and is contained in the union above, and since it avoids T the intersection with X is a closed subscheme of the affine scheme D_+(f), hence an affine open of X containing E.
proof_roadmap: Reduce all four cases to the case of a locally closed subscheme of a projective spectrum.
Cover the finite set by finitely many standard opens avoiding the complement.
Use the graded lemma to merge them into one standard open and read off the affine open of X.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if X is quasi-affine, or a locally closed subscheme of an affine scheme, or carries an ample invertible sheaf, or is a locally closed subscheme of a projective spectrum, then any finite subset of X lies in an affine open (statement lines 5460-5473). The proof (proof lines 5475-5507) reduces the cases to the projective one, covers the finite set by finitely many standard opens avoiding the complement, and merges them into a single standard open by a graded argument. H2: a reduction plus a two-step covering argument, written out in full.
